headline: Day Use and Camping Reservations for Georgian Bay Shorelines
reservation: Ontario Parks requires separate reservations for day-use vehicle permits and overnight campsites. Advanced booking windows for day use open five days prior to arrival, while campsites often book months in advance; verify current seasonal release dates through the official Ontario Parks portal before travel.

days.title: Granite Coastline and Windswept Pines

stops.name: Twin Points Trail
stops.detail: Walk through diverse ecosystems including beach, forest, and the signature smooth pink granite outcrops of the Canadian Shield.

stops.name: Harold Point
stops.detail: Observe the famous windswept white pines and geological formations that define the Georgian Bay landscape.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes for the drive and entry process; conditions vary by season.
days.note: Rocky surfaces can be slippery when wet; maintain distance from ledge edges.

days.title: Recreational Bays and Sound Views
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Killbear Park Mall

stops.name: Kilcoursie Bay
stops.detail: Relax at the park's largest sandy beach, ideal for viewing the expansive waters of the Big Sound.

stops.name: Lighthouse Point Trail
stops.detail: Follow the western tip of the peninsula to see the automated navigational light and panoramic water views.

days.driving: Internal park transit varies; allow 20 minutes between distant trailheads.
days.note: Black bears are active in this region; strictly follow all posted food storage regulations.

days.title: Regional Heritage and Waterfront

stops.name: Killbear Visitor Centre
stops.detail: Explore interactive exhibits regarding the Massasauga rattlesnake and the park's unique ecology.

stops.name: Blind Bay
stops.detail: Visit this sheltered area known for calmer waters and proximity to the park's eastern boundary.

days.driving: Allow 30-40 minutes for local transit; weekend traffic near the gatehouse may increase travel time.
days.note: The visitor centre has seasonal operating hours; check the park board for the daily schedule.

intel.title: Beach Access Parking
intel.text: Parking lots at Kilcoursie Bay fill rapidly during summer weekends. Consider arriving early or using the secondary lots near Harold Point if primary areas are at capacity.

intel.title: Cellular Connectivity
intel.text: Reception is generally stable near the main gate and Visitor Centre but can be intermittent in low-lying rocky coves. Download offline maps for the Parry Sound region prior to arrival.

intel.title: Gateway Supplies
intel.text: The last reliable fueling stations are located along Highway 69 or in Parry Sound. The Park Mall offers limited seasonal supplies but does not provide vehicle fuel.

intel.title: Seasonal Entry
intel.text: Autumn visits offer vibrant foliage but reduced services as campsites begin to close. Always verify if washroom facilities remain open after mid-October.

intel.title: Trail Surfaces
intel.text: Many routes involve traversing uneven granite rock. Sturdy footwear is recommended for the Lighthouse Point area where terrain is naturally rugged.

plan.arrival: Collect your vehicle at Sudbury Airport (YSB) and drive approximately two hours south to Parry Sound for grocery supplies and park permit validation.
plan.vehicle: Standard passenger cars are suitable for paved park roads; check rental agreements for restrictions on unpaved campground loops.
plan.goldenHour: Harold Point Rocks for sunset, though timing shifts significantly from June to September.
